title: Working with XML
learning_outcomes: Explain the role of working with xml in a Classic ASP application.
Identify and describe at least two syllabus subtopics: XML document structure and XML parsing concepts.
Inspect a minimal example and define a reproducible normal-case and failure-case test.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will study working with xml as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 83 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: Working with XML matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Classic ASP often relies on Windows COM components and external services for file operations, messaging, XML, and integration. For 'Working with XML', document the exact component/provider version, permissions, bitness, network boundaries, timeouts, and recovery behavior. Never construct a filesystem path or external URL directly from untrusted input, and keep secrets outside the public web root and repository.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: XML document structure; XML parsing concepts; Working with MSXML COM components; Reading XML values; XML validation considerations; Safe external-entity handling; XML integration in older applications. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Working with XML
content_blocks.code:
<%
Dim doc
Set doc = Server.CreateObject("MSXML2.DOMDocument.6.0")
doc.async = False
doc.resolveExternals = False
doc.setProperty "ProhibitDTD", True
If Not doc.Load("D:\CodeLeafData\sample.xml") Then
  Response.Write "XML could not be processed."
Else
  Response.Write Server.HTMLEncode(doc.documentElement.nodeName)
End If
Set doc = Nothing
%>

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Use approved test data and a component/service you control. Confirm path permissions, host allow-lists, timeouts, malformed responses, and cleanup behavior. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of working with xml. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming syntax alone proves the application works.
common_mistakes.why: IIS configuration, permissions, COM activation, database providers, and response behavior are external dependencies.
common_mistakes.fix: Run against the documented local test host and record exact evidence.
